resources.string: Native Dexcom ONE+ and G7 Bluetooth in AAPS. Apply the sensor, enter the pairing code immediately, then wait ~30 min warm-up before loop glucose.
Status, connect with pairing code, and warm-up
Apply sensor → enter code now → connect → ~30 min warm-up

How to start:
1. Apply the sensor on your body.
2. Paste the applicator Data Matrix (GS1) or enter the 4-digit pairing code — do not wait until after warm-up.
3. Stop Dexcom, xDrip, and Juggluco Direct (only one Bluetooth master).
4. Allow Bluetooth, Scan, select the highlighted sensor, then Connect / follow.
5. Accept the Android Bluetooth pairing prompt if shown.
6. Warm-up ~30 min for a new sensor; attaching to a running sensor can deliver EGVs sooner.
Connect adopts the selected sensor and opens the warm-up screen. The countdown also shows on the overview and in the ongoing notification — you do not have to stay on that screen.
Paste the full Data Matrix text from a QR scanner, or type the 4-digit PIN. Serial is stored for reconnect matching.

resources.string: Before pairing: allow nearby Bluetooth devices (and notifications if prompted). Keep the phone near the sensor during start and warm-up.
Scan for nearby ONE+ / G7-family sensors. Stop other Dexcom / xDrip / Juggluco Direct apps first.

Every ONE+ / G7 sensor in range is listed. The 4-digit code is not sent in the Bluetooth signal, so the app cannot use it to find your sensor. Pick the one you have just applied. The code is checked when you press Connect.
Select a sensor from the scan list
This is a different sensor from the paired one, but the pairing code has not changed. Paste the new applicator code — or press Connect again to keep the current one.

Stop the Dexcom app and xDrip first, because only one app can use the sensor over Bluetooth. This source attaches to a running sensor session and does not end it. It is not certain that the Dexcom app can use the sensor again afterwards.
Enter a valid 4-digit sensor pairing code
Bluetooth permission is required before starting the sensor

On: a finger prick value is sent to the sensor itself, as the Dexcom app does. The sensor keeps it for good and it cannot be edited or deleted. Off: the value is used to correct readings inside the app, and can be removed later.
The sensor accepts a finger prick value from 40 to 400 mg/dL (2.2 to 22.2 mmol/L) only.
This finger prick value is more than one hour old. Measure again.
The sensor is still warming up, or has stopped. Calibrate when it shows readings again.
No sensor reading in the last 10 minutes. Wait for the next reading, then try again.
The sensor did not give a trend with its last reading. Wait for the next reading, then try again.
Glucose is changing too fast. Calibrate when it is stable.
The value could not be sent to the sensor. The sensor may be out of range, still warming up, or another value may still be on its way.
No finger prick value has been sent to this sensor yet.
Your value is waiting to be sent to the sensor. It goes out the next time the app and the sensor talk, which is usually within a few minutes.
The sensor says it took your value.
The sensor says it did not take your value. Your reading was not changed.

The sensor did not give a clear answer, so it is not possible to say whether your value was used. It is not an app error and it is not a success. Do not send the value again. Compare the sensor with a finger prick within the next hour before you rely on its readings, and ask your care team if you are unsure.
Your value was not sent to the sensor. Nothing reached the sensor, so you can enter the value again.
The sensor or its connection changed before the value went out.

On by default. When "Create sensor change" is also on, a missing sensor change for the running sensor is written once, so the sensor age is right. An event you delete after that write is not written again.
Use a sensor change you logged as the start

On by default. When off, a new ONE+ session keeps the time of the start or of the first reading, and a sensor change logged earlier is not used to move that time back. When on, a sensor change from the last 24 hours that is earlier than that automatic time becomes the session start.
On by default. When on, the Status screen can move the insertion time of the sensor in use. Sensor change events between the old and the new time are invalidated. Calibration entries are not deleted.

Production feeds the loop after warm-up. Staging (pre-soak) warms a second sensor alongside the one you are currently using — it is collect-only and never feeds the loop until you promote it from the status screen.
The staging sensor collects readings in the background and does not feed the loop. Return to the overview; promote it later from the ONE+ / G7 status screen once it is ready.

This switches the loop\'s glucose source to the staging sensor and retires the sensor currently in use. This cannot be undone.
Use this only if the sensor in use has stopped or has to be replaced now. The new sensor is reading, but it has not finished its 12 hour settling time.
Switch to a sensor that is not settled?

The new sensor is sending readings, but it has not finished its 12 hour settling time. Its readings can be less accurate for the first hours, so the loop may dose on values that are too high or too low. Only do this if the sensor in use has stopped or must be replaced now. This switches the loop\'s glucose source and cannot be undone.
Staging sensor promoted — it now feeds the loop.
Sensor promoted, but older calibration entries could not be ignored. Remove fingerstick calibrations taken before this switch, then calibrate again if needed.
Sensor promoted, but reconnecting it failed. The production sensor is the one just promoted. Open the ONE+ status screen and bring the sensor back in range. This is not a complete success.
A step after the exchange failed, and the production sensor identity is missing. This is not a complete success. Open the ONE+ status screen and check which sensor is in use.
Staging sensor has not settled long enough to promote yet.
Staging sensor has not produced enough valid glucose yet.
Staging sensor has not sent a reading in the last minutes. Wait until it reads again before switching to it.
